answer: A burn registry prices every new agent identity in tokens it can never recover. Step one: a registrant burns 100 POA to a public address and the registry stamps the umber burn receipt with the device fingerprint. Step two: each later identity from that fingerprint pays double, so a tenth clone costs 51,200 POA. Step three: the burns are irrecoverable, so the ledger itself carries the price. Forging 10,000 identities drives a treasury to its nadir past 1,000,000 POA in fees, while an honest agent pays 100 once and voyages for years on one bond.
